task_metadata.research_topic: temporal frame-retention policy for autoregressive video generation
task_metadata.research_question: Design a better temporal frame-retention policy for autoregressive video generation under a fixed frame budget.
notes: The canonical FAR host-model paper was not returned by citation lookup, so the visible tests are linked to the nearest concrete video-generation and environment papers.
The recent_window baseline has no single canonical paper; it is linked approximately to StreamingLLM's window-attention / attention-sink family.

tests.label: ucf-short
tests.notes: UCF-101 short-prediction workload; linked to UCF-101 video-generation and future-prediction papers.

tests.label: ucf-scene-cut
tests.notes: UCF-101 scene-cut workload; linked to video-generation papers that study temporal prediction in natural video.

baselines.name: recent_window
baselines.notes: Naive sliding-window retention; mapped approximately to StreamingLLM because it explicitly studies window attention and KV cache retention.

papers.title: PackCache: A Training-Free Acceleration Method for Unified Autoregressive Video Generation via Compact KV-Cache
papers.relevance: Exact paper for the PackCache baseline used in this task.

papers.title: Flow caching for autoregressive video generation
papers.relevance: Exact paper for the FlowCache baseline; chunkwise adaptive caching is directly aligned with the task.

papers.title: Ca2-VDM: Efficient Autoregressive Video Diffusion Model with Causal Generation and Cache Sharing
papers.relevance: Exact paper for the CausalCache-VDM baseline.

papers.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
papers.relevance: Approximate link for the recent-window baseline; the paper studies window attention and KV retention under streaming constraints.

papers.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
